problem_statement: basehub-ai/help-center-template is a runnable Next.js App Router help center backed by the BaseHub CMS, with a Radix Themes shell: a top header with logo and Cmd+K search, a home page that greets the reader and lists help topics, category index pages that list their articles, article pages, dark/light theming, and responsive layout down to the 390px mobile viewport. Below the topic grid the home page hosts a native "Browse help articles by topic" finder: a row of topic pills (All topics plus one per help category) that filters a grid of real help articles and shows a live "Showing N of M · <topic>" result count; the same finder is also surfaced on every category page so a reader can jump across topics. The finder layout has REGRESSED and is visibly broken: the topic-pill row is locked to a fixed non-wrapping track far wider than the 390px mobile viewport (so every mobile finder state overflows horizontally), the article cards are pulled together with negative margins into a fixed narrow multi-column track so they shingle and OVERLAP each other with colliding, illegible text, and the selected topic pill has lost its fill so the active topic is a near-invisible chip. On top of the layout regression the finder has also been dropped from the category pages, so the cross-page browse affordance is missing there. Repair the topic finder so: the pill row wraps cleanly with no horizontal overflow on mobile; the article cards sit in a proper separated, legible grid with a clearly highlighted active pill; the finder is restored on the category pages; and the topic filter re-renders the article grid and the "Showing N of M · <topic>" count correctly on every click. Keep the BaseHub content, Radix styling, routes, external CMS assets, and all finder copy otherwise unchanged.
required_content: The "Browse help articles by topic" finder renders on the home page with a wrapping row of topic pills (All topics plus one per category) and a grid of real help-article cards, each showing its topic label, title and excerpt.
The finder is also present on every category page (the cross-page browse affordance), not only the home page.

The topic-pill row reflows so it no longer overflows the 390px mobile viewport on any captured mobile finder state, and the article cards sit in a cleanly separated, legible grid (no overlapping/shingled cards) with a clearly highlighted active pill.
Clicking a topic pill re-renders the article grid to that topic and updates the "Showing N of M · <topic>" readout to a value computed from the active topic (e.g. "Showing 3 of 6 · Team Management").
The BaseHub header/nav, Cmd+K search dialog, category and article routing, and remote CMS imagery remain reachable and unchanged.
design_constraints: Preserve the BaseHub Radix Themes design language: header, search dialog, category/article layout, color theme, and typography.
The repair is component-level and confined to the topic-finder component, its stylesheet, and the category-page wiring that mounts it; do not restructure routes or CMS queries.
The topic pills must wrap/reflow intentionally on mobile rather than being clipped or scrolled off-screen, and the article cards must not overlap.
The active topic pill must be visibly highlighted, and the result count must be derived from the currently selected topic (never a frozen snapshot).
state_constraints: desktop_initial/tablet_initial/mobile_initial capture the help center home at 1440/834/390px.
desktop_category/mobile_category capture the /getting-started category index (reference also shows the topic finder here).
desktop_finder/mobile_finder scroll the "Browse help articles by topic" finder into view on the home page showing all six article cards.
desktop_topic_filter/mobile_topic_filter click the Team Management topic pill on the home finder; the readout must read "Showing 3 of 6 · Team Management".

On the regressed baseline, the mobile finder states overflow horizontally because the topic-pill row is a fixed-width non-wrapping track wider than 390px, and the article cards overlap because they are shingled with negative margins; desktop does not overflow.

change_completion: The topic finder and all its topic pills and article cards render on the home page and on every category page.
Clicking a topic pill filters the article grid and updates the "Showing N of M · <topic>" count to the value computed for the active topic.
design_consistency: The repair preserves the BaseHub Radix header, search dialog, routing, theming, and typography.
The finder keeps its card and pill styling; the active pill is clearly highlighted and cards are cleanly separated.
regression: Home, category, and article routes and the Cmd+K search dialog remain reachable and render their content.
The Next.js build serves without runtime console errors.
responsive: The 390px mobile home finder and mobile topic-filter states have no horizontal overflow.
The topic pills wrap cleanly on mobile instead of being clipped or extending past the viewport.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js App Router + BaseHub CMS repair/component task on the help-center-template. The reference, baseline, and bad workspaces differ ONLY in the topic-finder component (app/_components/topic-finder/index.tsx), its stylesheet (app/_components/topic-finder/topic-finder.module.scss), and the category-page mount (app/[category]/page.tsx). The reference wraps the topic-pill row fluidly (flex-wrap:wrap) so no viewport overflows, lays the article cards out in a separated auto-fill grid, keeps a highlighted active pill, mounts the finder on both home and category pages, and derives the grid and "Showing N of M · <topic>" count from the active topic. The baseline is a genuine layout regression: the pill row is a fixed 720px non-wrapping track (mobile overflow ~540px), the article cards are shingled with negative margins so they overlap illegibly, the active pill loses its fill, and the finder is dropped from the category pages — but its topic filter wiring is still correct, so it filters the grid and count properly. The bad leg keeps the same broken layout AND freezes the visible article list and the count into initial useState snapshots, so clicking a topic pill toggles the active pill (the click genuinely succeeds) but the grid and the "Showing N of M" count never change — a stale-state defect. This is a repair regime with a native docs topic/article filter as the graded lever; the discriminators are no_horizontal_overflow on the mobile finder states, visual_regression on the finder crop, cross-page dom_assertions for the finder presence, and interaction_assertions on the filter readout. Imagery on the article route is served from assets.basehub.com.
